status: Nine expectations have source-fit authoring designs using unchanged shared claims and the specified dated resources. Other early-societies clauses remain under qualification; no pupil attainment or selection-readiness certification is inferred.

droulers-registry.kind: Heritage synthesis with an actual archaeological bone-tool photograph and physical-setting description
droulers-registry.selectedFacts: Mid-15th-century St Lawrence Iroquoian village; longhouse/storage/cooking traces; cultivated and wild food remains; stream/terrace setting.
droulers-registry.limits: Modern heritage synthesis and photograph of surviving objects, not an eyewitness village account. Possible exchange is not a proven trade itinerary. Avoid conflicting population/artefact counts as canonical knowledge, exact building dimensions and unassigned gender/status.

droulers-background.selectedFacts: Mid-15th-century occupation, food plants, fish/cooking and material-object evidence.
droulers-background.limits: Shares the excavation evidence and institution with the registry; two publications are not two independent excavations.

droulers-centre.selectedFacts: Approximately 1450 village and modern longhouse/garden interpretation.
droulers-centre.limits: Label reconstructed views and the source’s dating. Do not make a current reconstruction an original photograph or settle modern citizenship from a broad historical label.

qari-site.kind: Published archaeological research, selected printed pp. 165–175; figure 11.1 on printed p. 167
qari-site.selectedFacts: Qariaraqyuk, southeast Somerset Island, substantial 14th-century occupation; winter-house depressions, seasonal structures, storage and marine-harvest evidence; 1992 survey plan.
qari-site.limits: Only selected appropriate material is used. The plan is a modern archaeological record, not a map made by the early community. Household/political reconstructions using later analogies are labelled models, not direct observation. Exclude adult violent/sexual passages from the child packet.

qari-synthesis.kind: Author-hosted 2016 uncorrected chapter proof, selected pp. 825–827
qari-synthesis.selectedFacts: Seasonal winter/warm-weather dwelling forms, distinct communities and Qariaraqyuk house clusters; place/material context for the published site account.
qari-synthesis.limits: Explicitly an uncorrected proof and synthesis by the same researcher, not independently verified final publisher text or an eyewitness source. Broad Arctic patterns do not assign every practice to every person or site.

egypt-painting-notes.kind: Museum source notes, copyright 2024; all nine pages read
egypt-painting-notes.selectedFacts: Nebamun, Thebes, around 1350 BCE; marsh/boat/bird/fish representation, estate/worker images and why tomb paintings idealise a wealthy official’s life/afterlife.
egypt-painting-notes.limits: Not a photograph of an ordinary household or proof every Egyptian had the same life. Do not substitute reconstructed complete scenes for the surviving fragment or import modern daily life.

egypt-painting.kind: British Museum collection partner account and actual viewed image of EA37977
egypt-painting.selectedFacts: Surviving painted fragment with a boat, marsh plants, birds, fish and represented family; institution attributes it around 1350 BCE.
egypt-painting.limits: The primary object is the surviving painting; the photograph and museum explanation are modern. Its purpose and elite viewpoint limit any daily-life inference.

egypt-evidence.kind: Harvard Giza Project explanation of archaeological and art evidence
egypt-evidence.selectedFacts: Food production/preparation/storage and craft activities are represented in material/art evidence; tomb scenes had an afterlife purpose and do not supply a complete picture.
egypt-evidence.limits: Method/context synthesis, not an independent eyewitness account of Nebamun or every Egyptian period.

egypt-geography.kind: University museum resource, selected geography pp. 6–9 and daily-life pp. 28–32
egypt-geography.selectedFacts: Nile water/floodplain/silt links with agriculture/materials; separate dated Dynastic housing and Roman-period Karanis evidence.
egypt-geography.limits: Use only verified selected facts, with era labels. The raw p. 76 Upper/Lower Egypt label placement is unreliable and is excluded. Roman-period toys/objects are not backdated to the 1350 BCE painting. No universal diet, modern hydrology or first-invention claim.

performanceConditions.thirdSociety: Egypt, with explicit different case/period labels
performanceConditions.inquiryFocus: Interrelationships between local environment and ways of life

preparation: Prepare original age-appropriate summaries with actual source/place/period labels, lawful linked visual evidence and both printed and digital source encounters. The source texts remain available for teacher checking; a generic source-name list alone is insufficient. Do not reproduce restricted curriculum wording or unlicensed images in this public report.

Include the mid-15th-century Droulers village, the substantially 14th-century Qariaraqyuk community and the differently situated Egyptian material. All three must actually enter the inquiry, not merely appear in a resource list. Distinguish the First Nation and early Inuit cases, their approximate dates and cultural/archaeological labels.

Prepare a legible original broad world locator/globe reference with the three actual named settings and declared orientation. From source-supported facts, prepare a thematic key for the local river/stream or marine access, documented food production/harvest and dwelling/material features. This is an explicitly approximate teaching representation, not a surveyed pre-1500 territory, identical shoreline reconstruction or map of every people’s land. Exclude the unreliable raw Kelsey p. 76 region labels; verify any physical/location feature before carrying it into the original reference.

Use the actual Droulers bone-tool photograph, the actual Qariaraqyuk 1992 survey plan/key and the actual British Museum partner image of the surviving Nebamun fragment. Separate object/remain, modern record/photograph, historical account and reconstruction. A supplied modern longhouse reconstruction is a comparison of evidence roles, not direct proof of every old building detail.
actions: Formulate three genuine questions about environment and ways of life: how Droulers food/material evidence connects to its setting; how Qariaraqyuk seasonal homes/storage connect with marine access; and what Egyptian visual/material evidence can and cannot show about local resources and daily life. Include who/what/where/when/why questions about an actual old object/image and a supported past/present place question. The learner may refine these questions rather than repeat teacher wording.

For each question identify and use two named sources: Droulers registry plus 2016 backgrounder; Qariaraqyuk published site research plus the explicitly labelled author proof; and British Museum painting/notes plus Harvard evidence explanation or the selected Kelsey geography section. Explain shared underlying evidence/author/institution where relevant; two views of the same webpage are not two sources. Take brief organised notes from an actual printed source and actual digital material, sorting case, period, food/home/material, setting connection, evidence and uncertainty. Write an original summary combining two sources.

Analyse the broad location and environmental thematic references. Locate all three studied settings, read keys/labels and extract supported water/material/food relationships. Interpret the Qariaraqyuk survey key for actual winter-house/storage features and the source’s uncertainty. Construct an original print or digital thematic map with labels/key showing the studied setting relationships, distinguishing supplied source information from an inference. Do not require formal scale calculation or invent precise historical boundaries.

Retain the whole familiar-environment map operation: make an above-view class or familiar-place map with a key/labels, position landmarks relative to one another and describe a route. Apply the same representation operation to the prepared historical references; success on a single plotted point does not establish that whole claim.

Use a comparison table, annotated source image and thematic map to analyse the information. From the Droulers tool photograph describe observable material/shape features and cautiously infer a supported possible use with catalogue context; do not assign a gender or exact use from shape alone. From Qariaraqyuk’s archaeological plan extract housing/storage clues; from Nebamun’s fragment extract represented boat/plants/animals and distinguish visible features from the supplied elite/afterlife interpretation. Explain why absent or selectively surviving records leave some lives less visible.

Compare the Droulers heritage/interpretation accounts: identify agreement on approximate period and farming/village evidence, and the differing population estimates presented by the sources. The estimates are supplied for a source-comparison task, not memorised historical knowledge. Suggest why estimates or different dated summaries might differ, label the actual cause unresolved unless verified, and reject a population-growth story unsupported by those estimates. Explain why repeated descriptions from shared excavations do not independently settle an exact number.

Draw an evidence-supported answer to each original question and a cross-case environmental relationship conclusion, retaining differences and uncertainty. Make a bounded prediction about what an additional documented storage or food-remain find might help test; state it is a research expectation, not a fact about an unexcavated site. Suggest a concrete inquiry improvement such as checking an additional properly attributed excavation record or clarifying a map/source label. No invented ecological impact or cultural hierarchy.

Communicate the inquiry with an original organised oral report and a brief written explanation/annotated map. Use relevant actual case words accurately (for example, longhouse, storage, winter dwelling, cultivated plant, source, reconstruction), not an exhaustive official example inventory. The oral report includes at least three organised supported facts, clear descriptive details and an understandable pace; review a recording or live feedback for clarity and details. For the existing recounting operation, explain the investigation’s own sequence with a beginning, middle and end. Produce an original summary rather than copy captions.

Use a new attributed visual or changed-view locator to transfer the evidence/map/comparison operation. Keep a fresh source’s information supplied and distinguish it from remembered case knowledge. No new topic or inferred pupil mastery follows from a completed authoring protocol.
nearMiss: Only one Indigenous case actually used while the other is listed in the packet.
Reads only digital summaries or treats a repeated URL as a second source.
Copies a completed thematic map or locates points without extracting an environmental relationship.
Uses a modern staged longhouse, 1992 plan or Roman-period toy as an original 1450/1350 BCE image.
Treats elite afterlife art or analogy-based social modelling as the observed daily life of every person.
Makes a decorative graph, infers historic population trends from different modern estimates or invents a detailed trade route.

limits: Only selected source sections and the named actual visuals were checked; no whole long-volume or unseen gallery verification is claimed.
Source-fit authoring is not a learner observation or teaching-efficacy result.
The approved early-community knowledge claim stays bounded; this protocol does not create new factual claims or rewrite old cards.

readinessBoundary.note: Existing hard paths include English question/inference and historical vocabulary, familiar-place positioning, and a chart-producing data path beneath the shared conclusion topic. The source-fit design does not certify those separate whole claims, insert unrelated graphs, broaden eligibility or create prerequisite source associations. These are explicit consumer/readiness or future edge-review questions, not missing historical topics.
